title: Rock Elementalist
personality:
A young, nimble rock elementalist with a bandana tied over his eyes. He reads the ground by feel.
Quiet and light on his feet, he moves stone like it is a dance partner.
fantasy: The quarry-hand. Raises stone out of the ground, climbs it, then punches it into you.
silhouette: the stone shoulder and the huge molten-cracked fists

card.role: Brawler and builder: raises rocks to climb and hide behind, then punches them into the enemy.
card.loop: Brawler and builder: raises rocks to climb and hide behind, then punches them into the enemy.
card.lmb: Rubble Fists: tap to throw a boulder; hold and let go to punch everything in the lane, and every rock in it flies.
card.rmb: Quakefall: hold to gather, let go to hop and slam; the centre stuns. Jump while holding to leap forward.
card.e: Stone Row: raise three rocks ahead. Stand on them, climb them, or punch them into foes.
card.dash: Rubble Leap: leap to the cursor and land with a crash; the rock you leapt from follows, then rolls on and slows.
card.x: Basalt Spine: from level 6, raise a long ridge of rocks at the cursor; hold and drag to turn it. Rocks only rise on solid ground.
card.passive: Molten Guard: punching your own rocks gives you a shield. Tremor Sense: sneak to see enemies in a cone ahead through walls; it widens as you sneak.

weapons.rubble_fists: Tap to throw a boulder; hold and let go to punch everything in the lane, and every rock in it flies.

passive.name: Molten Guard
passive.desc: Molten Guard: a punch that sends any of your rocks flying gives you a shield of 18, up to 4 stacks for 6s (one stack per punch, however many rocks it throws). Tremor Sense: while sneaking, a narrow cone ahead (25 degrees, widening to 40 over 2s of sneaking, 16m long) shows every enemy in it through walls and fog as a molten ring, refreshed every half second.

dash.name: Rubble Leap
dash.desc: A rock bursts up under you and you leap to the cursor (up to about 4m). You land with a crash that shoves everyone beside you, and the rock comes down right after you and rolls on 6m: 12 damage, a shove, Shred (+15% damage taken for 3s) and a 1.5s slow. In the air: your long dash.

variants.tap: A quick hop and slam just ahead: 14 damage and a shove, the centre stuns, rocks in the ring fly outward.
variants.hold: Hold up to 1.2s: a bigger, harder slam (up to 30) whose growing centre stuns up to 1.2s. Jump while holding to leap forward; punch to lunge.
variants.air: In the air you dive, and slam where you land; pressed while gliding, the glider folds and you plunge. A foe caught in the air is spiked down for +40%, +20 more over the abyss.

e.name: Stone Row
e.desc: A red flash on the ground, then three rocks rise in a slight curve 3.4m ahead, spanning 5m (on solid ground only, never into bodies). They stop foes and shots, hold 9s, you can stand on and climb them, and any punch, slam or dash-launch sends them flying.

x.name: Basalt Spine
x.desc: Tap: a ridge of 13 rocks, 19.8m long, centred at the cursor (up to 11m away) and across your aim. Hold the key and drag the cursor to swing it round its centre; let go to cast. Molten cracks show along the line for 0.2s, then the rocks erupt from the centre outward over 0.4s, slowing foes beside them by 35% for 1s and shoving anyone on the line aside. They are your rocks for 7s: they stop foes and their shots, you stand on them and climb them, and a punch along the ridge launches the whole line (its rocks deal at most 40 to any one hunter). Rocks only rise on solid ground: the ridge stops at the abyss, and with no ground under it the cast is refused. 45s.

rank3.sec: slamming a foe or a rock gives a Molten Guard shield of 18, up to 4 stacks
rank3.dash: a second charge, and the leap goes a third further
rank3.kin: an extra row of rocks behind the first

rank_next.sec: Rank 3: cooldown 9s -> 7.2s, damage +30%; slamming a foe or a rock gives a shield of 18, up to 4 stacks.
rank_next.kin: Rank 3: cooldown 13s -> 10.4s; an extra row of rocks behind the first.
rank_next.dash: Rank 3: recharge 12s -> 8.4s; a second charge, and the leap goes a third further.

tells.half: stone pebbles orbit the shoulder, one per live rock
